case: Madras Bar Association v. Union of India
issue: Whether the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021 could re-enact provisions previously invalidated by the Court.
ruling: The Court invalidated key restrictions and held that legislation cannot simply override a judgment without curing the constitutional defect.

case: Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay v. Union of India (hate speech)
issue: Whether courts may create or expand criminal offences through directions where legislation does not do so.
ruling: The Court declined the requested intervention, treating creation of criminal offences and punishments as a legislative function.

case: Supriyo @ Supriya Chakraborty v. Union of India
issue: Whether the Court could extend marriage recognition under the Special Marriage Act to same-sex couples.
ruling: The Court left creation of a new marriage or civil-union framework to legislative policy.

case: Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay v. Union of India (minimum age of marriage)
issue: Whether the minimum age of marriage for women should be raised to 21 to match that for men.
ruling: The Court declined to direct Parliament to establish a uniform minimum age.

case: Sanjay Prakash v. Union of India (CAPF, OGAS)
issue: Whether executive service and promotion policies in the CAPFs complied with constitutional requirements.
ruling: The Court used judicial review to address restrictions affecting service equality and highlighted limits on executive action.

case: Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Limited v. Amit Gupta
issue: How the IBC tribunal's jurisdiction applies to disputes involving contracts and regulatory matters.
ruling: The Court clarifying jurisdictional boundaries among tribunals, contracts, and courts.

case: In Re: Special Reference No. 1 of 2025 (Governors, Articles 200 and 201)
issue: What limits govern a Governor's options when considering State bills.
ruling: The Court described limits on gubernatorial inaction and addressed the relationship between executive and legislative roles.

case: Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India
issue: How the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners should be appointed in the absence of legislation.
ruling: The Court prescribed an interim appointment committee arrangement until Parliament enacted a law.

case: Animal Welfare Board of India v. Union of India (Jallikattu)
issue: Whether State amendments permitting Jallikattu were valid after the Court's earlier decision.
ruling: The Court upheld the amendments, treating them as changing the legal framework considered earlier.

case: Government of NCT of Delhi v. Union of India (Services)
issue: Which government controls services in the National Capital Territory of Delhi.
ruling: The Court recognized a significant role for Delhi's elected government in administration and discussed federal boundaries.

case: Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India (Electoral Bonds)
issue: Whether the Electoral Bond Scheme and related amendments were constitutionally valid.
ruling: The Court invalidated the scheme on rights grounds, while recognizing that legislation remains subject to judicial review.

case: Cox & Kings Ltd. v. SAP India Pvt. Ltd.
issue: How the group-of-companies doctrine applies under Indian arbitration law.
ruling: The Court addressed interpretation of corporate relationships while applying the governing statutory framework.

case: Subhash Desai v. Principal Secretary, Governor of Maharashtra
issue: Whether the Governor could call for a trust vote based on internal party disputes and how the Speaker's role applied.
ruling: The Court found the floor-test decision unlawful but declined to restore the former Chief Minister after his resignation.

case: Neil Aurelio Nunes v. Union of India (NEET OBC/EWS)
issue: Whether the reservation policy for OBC and EWS candidates in NEET was subject to judicial intervention.
ruling: The Court upheld the policy and described limits on judicial review of policy choices.

case: Pankaj Bansal v. Union of India
issue: What safeguards apply to arrest powers exercised by enforcement authorities under the PMLA.
ruling: The Court required written communication of the grounds of arrest as a check on executive power.

case: Central Electricity Regulatory Commission v. NTPC
issue: How far courts may intervene in tariff decisions made by expert regulatory bodies.
ruling: The Court emphasized deference to technical expertise and cautioned against courts setting tariffs.

case: S. G. Vombatkere v. Union of India (Sedition)
issue: How Section 124A of the Indian Penal Code should be treated while its constitutionality was challenged.
ruling: The Court stayed enforcement temporarily and asked the Union to reconsider the provision.

case: State of Punjab v. Principal Secretary to Governor
issue: Whether the Governor could question the validity of an Assembly session when considering bills passed by it.
ruling: The Court held that the Governor could not question the session's validity and stressed the functioning of the elected legislature.

case: In Re: Section 6A of the Citizenship Act
issue: Whether Parliament had competence to enact Section 6A and whether the provision was constitutional.
ruling: The Court upheld Section 6A and recognized Parliament's latitude in citizenship matters.
